About us

Bitget is the world's largest Universal Exchange (UEX), serving over 125 million users and offering access to over 2M crypto tokens, 100+ tokenized stocks, ETFs, commodities, FX, and precious metals such as gold. The ecosystem is committed to helping users trade smarter with its AI agent, which co-pilots trade execution.

Bitget is driving crypto adoption through strategic partnerships with LALIGA and MotoGP™. Aligned with its global impact strategy, Bitget has joined hands with UNICEF to support blockchain education for 1.1 million people by 2027. Bitget currently leads in the tokenized TradFi market, providing the industry's lowest fees and highest liquidity across 150 regions worldwide.

Role Overview
We are looking for a Market Research Manager to join the Product Marketing Strategy function. This role is the center of excellence for market intelligence — responsible for generating actionable insights that inform product direction, go-to-market strategy, brand positioning, and growth initiatives. You will own the research agenda end to end, from desk research through commissioning and managing third-party vendors for both quantitative and qualitative studies.

Key Responsibilities
Market & Competitive Intelligence
• Conduct ongoing desk research to track market trends, emerging technologies, regulatory shifts, and macro-economic signals.
• Deliver structured competitor analysis, The product features comparisons, positioning shifts, pricing models, and go-to-market moves.
• Produce market sizing and forecasting to support strategic planning and annual business reviews.

Brand & Consumer Research
• Design, brief, and manage third-party quantitative research (surveys, brand trackers, U&A studies, NPS/CSAT measurement).
• Lead qualitative research projects (focus groups, in-depth interviews, ethnographies) in partnership with specialist agencies.
• Own the brand health tracking framework : Defines KPIs, manage fielding cadence, synthesizes wave-over-wave trends into actionable recommendations.

Product Deep-Dive & Opportunity Identification
• Lead product deep-dive analyses: evaluate feature adoption, usage patterns, and competitive alternatives to identify gaps and optimization points.
• Identify white-space opportunities where unmet user needs intersect with business capability.
• Partner with Product Management to inform the product roadmap with evidence-based user insights.

Audience & Messaging
• Drive audience segmentation projects: define personas, segment value propositions, and prioritize target cohorts.
• Support user messaging and positioning development through message testing, value-proposition validation, and perceptual mapping.
• Enable the broader marketing team with insight-backed briefs for campaigns, creative development, and content strategy.

Performance & Funnel Measurement
• Design and maintain performance tracking frameworks — brand funnel, conversion funnel, awareness → consideration → preference → action.
• Partner with Data & Analytics teams to align primary research outputs with behavioral data (CRM, web analytics, product telemetry).
• Deliver periodic research readouts that connect findings to business outcomes and inform leadership decision-making.

Who You Are
Essential Qualifications
• Experience: 5–8 years in market research, consumer insights, or strategy roles, agency or in-house side both considered.
• Research methods: Deep understanding of quantitative methodology (sampling, questionnaire design, statistical significance, crosstab analysis) and qualitative methodology (moderation guides, thematic analysis, projective techniques).
• Desk research fluency: Able to independently synthesize secondary sources (industry reports, analyst publications, academic journals, patent databases) into concise intelligence briefs.
• Vendor management: Proven experience briefing, managing, and QC'ing third-party research agencies — on time, on budget, on quality.
• Storytelling with data: Ability to translate complex data sets into clear, persuasive narratives for senior stakeholders.

Preferred Qualifications
• Experience in Web 3, Fintech or traditional finance
• Familiarity with brand tracking platforms (e.g., Brandwatch, YouGov, Kantar) and survey tools (Qualtrics, SurveyMonkey, Confirmit).
• Exposure to behavioral science or advanced analytics (conjoint analysis, MaxDiff, TURF, K-means clustering).
• Experience working in cross-functional teams alongside Product, Brand, and Growth functions.
• Fluent in AI and data modeling tools

Why Bitget?

• We are a global company with staff members from over 50 different countries and regions
• We are growing and looking for world-class ambitious talents to help us continue this journey
• We have a streamlined structure that empowers employees to work efficiently, delivering the best results in a short timeframe
• We offer competitive salaries and benefits
• Blockchain technology and digital assets have the potential to change finance in a way no other technology can - be part of it!

If you are ambitious and believe that digital assets could be the next financial and technological revolution, please apply!

In 2018, Bitvavo launched the first version of its digital assets trading platform, to bridge the gap between traditional currencies and digital assets. By offering transparent fees, a wide range of assets and an easy to use platform, Bitvavo is making the currency of the future accessible for everyone.

In eight years time, Bitvavo has established itself as the market leader in the Netherlands and one of the largest in Europe, with over two million users exchanging tens of billions of digital assets a year.


ABOUT THE OPPORTUNITY

We are an exchange. The speed of good decisions matter in everything that we do. Our data domain is committed to making sure the decisions this business makes on spend, pricing, product, risk and financial crime rest on evidence rather than intuition. We're seeking exceptional talent to join us in making this a reality.



The Problems You'll Get to Solve

 - Growth & causal inference. Measure true incrementality, own our marketing mix model, and turn that into spend allocation under a budget.

 - Product & personalization. Rank and surface what is relevant to each customer's behaviour and holdings, from asset discovery to order form defaults, without drowning users in noise

 - Markets, pricing & execution. Model fee and spread elasticity to find the revenue-versus-volume trade-off, and improve execution quality: slippage, order routing, liquidity provider selection.

 - Risk & financial integrity. Model risk exposure across a volatile asset book, forecast liquidation risk, and detect reconciliation breaks across internal ledgers, on-chain data and partner reporting.

 - Financial crime & compliance. Detect account takeover, payment fraud and mule networks in real time, combining business rules and models that work together while staying explainable and auditable.



What You'll Be Doing

 - Own problems end to end: frame the question with the stakeholder, build the model or experiment, ship it, and follow it into production.

 - Work backwards from the decision. Start from what someone needs to decide and what it costs to get it wrong, not from the data that happens to be available.

 - Stay accountable for your models once they are live: monitoring, drift, retraining, and the day they start behaving differently.

 - Tell senior stakeholders things they do not want to hear, including that a campaign, a feature or a rule did not work.

 - Support your teammates in growing every day by setting the standard for how we do causal inference, reviewing their work, and sharing knowledge.



What We Look For

 - Strong applied experience turning a messy business question into a model or a measurement: causal inference where that fits, predictive and ranking models where it does not. You know when a result is not real.

 - Fluency in Python and SQL, and comfort working independently rather than waiting for data to be handed to you. We use Snowflake, dbt, Airflow and Looker, on top of technologies like MySQL, Druid, Kafka and Flink.

 - A track record of models that made it into production and changed a decision, not just notebooks and slide decks.

BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE


Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.






THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. Offering spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.




Kraken Pro is where serious traders work. Tight spreads, deep books, an API people actually build on. The people who use it are demanding, opinionated, and allergic to marketing.




We want someone who belongs in that room. Not a brand account with a person behind it, but a trader's trader who happens to be very good at building community.




Come here to build and grow this Community for us.




THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Live in the trenches. Discord, Telegram, X, TradingView, Reddit, the group chats you're already in at 3am. You're not "monitoring channels". You're a participant, with standing.

 - Be the fastest voice in the room. When a chain halts, a listing drops, or the market goes vertical, you're posting before the screenshots start circulating. Speed with accuracy, not vibes.

 - Build the inner circle. Stand up an ambassador and power-user program: the market makers, quant desks, and high-volume traders who'll tell you the truth about the product. Give them a reason to stay loud.

 - Run the room in public. AMAs, live trading sessions, feature launches, competitions, post-mortems when we get something wrong. Own the format, don't just attend it.

 - Close the loop with Product. You'll be the first to hear that the order entry flow is broken. Your job is to get it to the PM with receipts, then go back and tell the community what happened.

 - Write things people screenshot. Threads on microstructure, teardowns of new features, release notes that don't read like release notes.

 - Prove it worked. Sentiment, share of voice, community-sourced signups, retention of the accounts that matter. You bring the numbers to the table before anyone asks.




WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - You trade. Actual positions, actual scars. You can hold a conversation about funding rates, maker/taker economics, slippage, and latency without reaching for a glossary.

 - 3+ years running community or social for a product with a technical, skeptical audience. Crypto, fintech, gaming, or dev tools all count.

 - You write fast and well. Short-form that lands, long-form that holds up under scrutiny from people smarter than the average follower.

 - You have thick skin and good instincts. Crypto community management means getting yelled at with an audience watching. You de-escalate without going corporate and you know when to push back.

 - You've built something from a standing start, not just maintained an existing account.

 - You operate without a brief. Markets don't wait for approval chains, and neither should you… because you know where the line is and you don't need a committee to find it.

 - You're comfortable with the ambiguity of a company that ships constantly and reorganizes around opportunity.



Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.




OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.


We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.


As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.



Stay connected

Follow us on X https://twitter.com/krakenfx

Learn on the Kraken Blog https://blog.kraken.com/#:~:text=Enter%20your%20email%20address

Connect on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/kraken-exchange/

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a local Head of Risk role, based in Limassol, owning risk management for Bitvavo Europe Limited, our MiFID II regulated entity in Cyprus and reporting to our Group Head of Risk in Amsterdam.

As this is a local role, we are only considering candidates who are currently based in Cyprus and able to work from Limassol.




WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING

Enterprise Risk and Governance

 - Own and continuously improve the risk management framework, including risk taxonomy, risk appetite, tolerance levels, risk register, policies, RCSA methodology and the three-lines-of-defence operating model

 - Maintain the risk appetite framework across credit, market, solvency, liquidity, operational, reputational, strategic and technology risk

 - Produce concise, decision-oriented reporting for the Board and Risk Committee, covering the risk tolerance dashboard, top risks, appetite breaches, emerging themes and open issues

 - Support the Board's annual assessment of framework effectiveness and respond to Internal Audit and CySEC findings within the function's remit

Financial Risk

 - Counterparty and credit: Monitor exposure to clients, clearing members, CCPs, bilateral counterparties and custodians, including limits, concentration analysis and collateral

 - Client margin and leverage: Conduct independent review of margin methodology, define stress tests, set tolerance levels and gap risk on derivatives and leveraged products, and challenge assumptions and back test outcomes

 - Market risk: Manage inventory, hedging, settlement mismatches, FX and corporate action exposure, within set sensitivity and position limits

 - Liquidity and funding: Oversee settlement liquidity, cash funding for settlement purposes, liquidity stress testing and the contingency funding plan

 - Capital: Own the ICARA, including own funds and K factor monitoring, internal capital and liquidity adequacy, and wind down analysis, supporting accurate prudential reporting to CySEC

 - Stress testing: Run firm wide and reverse stress tests covering extreme market moves, gap events, venue or CCP disruption, clearing broker default and volume spikes, with clear management actions

Non-Financial Risk

 - Third party and outsourcing: Conduct criticality assessment, due diligence, concentration risk analysis, exit strategies and maintenance of the register of arrangements

About Uphold

Uphold is a financial technology company that believes on-chain services are the future of finance. We provide modern infrastructure for on-chain payments, banking and investments. Offering Consumer Services, Business Services and Institutional Trading, Uphold makes pioneering financial services easy and trusted for millions of customers in more than 140 countries.

Uphold integrates with over 30 trading venues, including centralized and decentralized exchanges, to deliver superior liquidity and optimal execution. Uphold never loans out customer assets and is always 100% reserved. The company pioneered radical transparency and uniquely publishes its assets and liabilities every 30 seconds on our public website Transparency Page

Uphold strips away the complexity to open up Web3 finance for everyone.

To learn more about Uphold, please visit https://uphold.com.

Job Summary

Uphold is looking for Marketing Technology Manager, CRM Platform a to take full ownership of Customer.io, the platform we use to communicate with millions of customers across email, push, in-app and SMS.

This is a technical role, not a campaign execution role. You will own the data model, the integrations, the workflow architecture and the operating standards that make customer communication possible at scale. You will sit between Engineering, Data, Marketing and Commercial, and you will be the person who decides how the platform is built and how it is used.

The scope is wide. Uphold runs multiple products and regions on shared infrastructure, in a highly regulated industry, with a large volume of personal data. Getting this right means designing for reuse, for auditability and for safety, not just for the next campaign.

What you’ll be doing primarily

Own the CRM data foundation

• Own the data layer inside Customer.io: Define and maintain the objects, attributes, events and identifiers that power the platform. Segmentation quality is a direct function of data quality, so this is the core of the role.

• Work hand in hand with Engineering and Data: Design and maintain the pipelines that feed Customer.io. Agree on schemas, event contracts and data freshness requirements, and hold the line when they drift.

• Guarantee freshness and correctness: Put monitoring and alerting in place so that stale, missing or malformed data is caught before it reaches a customer, not after.

Architect workflows that last

• Apply systems thinking to campaign design: Build journeys, triggers and segments that are modular, reusable and understandable by someone who did not build them.

• Prevent workflow sprawl: Establish naming conventions, versioning, documentation and deprecation routines. Retire what is no longer used. Treat the CRM workspace as a codebase, not a folder of one off campaigns.

• Design for scale: Anticipate volume, message throughput, rate limits and platform constraints before they become production issues.

Operate with a multi product and multi brand mindset

• Serve several products and brands from one platform: Design workspace structure, data models and templates so that Wallet, Topper, Enterprise and future brands share what should be shared and separate what must be separated.

• Balance consistency with autonomy: Give each product team room to move without letting the overall architecture fragment.

• Manage cross brand message pressure: Own global frequency capping, priority rules and suppression logic so customers receive a coherent experience across products.

Translate business objectives into CRM capability

• Partner with Marketing and Commercial: Understand what the business is trying to achieve, then decide what the platform needs to look like to support it. Push back when a request is better solved a different way.

• Turn requirements into architecture: Convert commercial goals into concrete data, segmentation and workflow design, with clear trade offs and sequencing.

• Own the roadmap for the platform: Maintain a prioritised view of platform work and communicate it to stakeholders.

Enable marketing autonomy

• Build for self sufficiency: Create templates, reusable components, documented segments and clear guardrails so marketing teams can launch routine work without engineering support.

• Train and document: Run enablement sessions and maintain practical documentation. Success is measured by how much the teams can do without you, not by how much depends on you.

• Set the guardrails: Define what marketers can change freely, what needs review, and what is locked. Make the safe path the easy path.

Drive automation and AI adoption

• Identify automation opportunities: Look for manual, repetitive or error prone steps across the CRM operation and remove them.

• Apply AI where it earns its place: Evaluate and implement AI for content generation, send time and channel optimisation, segmentation, anomaly detection and QA. Be pragmatic about where it adds value and where it does not.

• Keep improving the operation: Measure the cycle time from business request to live campaign, and work it down.

Security and data protection first

• Treat personal data with care: This is a PII heavy environment. Apply data minimisation, least privilege access, retention rules and clear handling standards by default.

• Own consent and preferences: Maintain the consent, opt out and preference model, and make sure it is respected consistently across every channel and every brand.

• Support compliance and audit: Work with Security, Privacy, Compliance and Legal on GDPR, access reviews, vendor risk and audit evidence. Be able to explain who received what, when, and on what basis.

• Respect jurisdictional rules: Uphold operates under multiple regulatory regimes. Build the targeting and suppression logic that keeps communications compliant by market, including mandatory risk warnings and geographic restrictions on financial promotions.

Protect quality at the customer touchpoint

• Be detail and quality obsessed: Every message is a direct customer touchpoint and a reflection of the brand. Own the QA process, including test sends, seed lists, rendering checks, link validation and pre send review.

• Own deliverability: Manage domain and IP reputation, authentication (SPF, DKIM, DMARC), warm up, list hygiene, bounce and complaint rates. Deliverability is an engineering problem, and it belongs to this role.

• Run change management: Define approval gates, no send windows, rollback procedures and incident response for communication failures.

• Measure and improve: Own experimentation design, holdout groups and performance reporting, in partnership with the Data team.

Required Qualifications and Skills

• BS or advanced degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering or equivalent practical experience.

• 4+ years of experience in the field, with meaningful time spent owning a marketing automation, CRM or customer engagement platform in a technical capacity.

• Hands-on experience with Customer.io, or a comparable platform such as Braze, Iterable, Klaviyo or Salesforce Marketing Cloud, at an architecture and administration level rather than campaign execution only.

• Strong SQL and comfort working with data warehouses and modern data pipelines.

• Solid understanding of REST APIs, webhooks, event driven data models and identity resolution.

• Working knowledge of templating languages such as Liquid, plus HTML, CSS and JavaScript for email and in-app content.

• Demonstrated systems thinking: the ability to design maintainable, scalable structures rather than solve each request in isolation.

• Experience working with personal data under a security and privacy first approach, including consent management and GDPR.

• Ability to explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non technical audiences.

• Comfortable working across functions with Marketing, Commercial, Product, Data and Engineering.

• Strong sense of ownership, accountability and attention to detail.

• Fluent written and oral English.

Salary: $150K + Bonus, Benefits

Bonus if you have

• Experience in fintech, financial services or another regulated industry.

• Familiarity with cryptocurrencies or other digital assets, as they are core to our business.

• Experience running CRM across multiple products or brands from a single platform.

The Role:
As a Transaction Monitoring Investigator, you will play a critical role in safeguarding the integrity of the Bitfinex platform by identifying, investigating, and mitigating financial crime risks across both fiat and cryptocurrency transactions. Working within the Compliance team, you will analyze transaction monitoring alerts, assess unusual account activity, and investigate potential money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions, and fraud-related risks using a risk-based approach. You will collaborate closely with AML Investigators, Product teams, and Compliance leadership to ensure timely escalation of high-risk cases, contribute to regulatory reporting and process improvements, and continuously enhance monitoring controls. This role requires strong analytical thinking, sound judgment, and a deep interest in cryptocurrency, blockchain transactions, and evolving AML/KYC regulations within a fast-paced global fintech environment.

Your Day-to-Day:
•
Develop and implement transaction monitoring algorithms to monitor for anti-money laundering, terrorism financing, sanctions and other compliance risks to enable controls to be implemented to mitigate against detected risks using a risk-based approach.
•
Analyze and investigate alerts generated by the transaction monitoring system arising from fiat money (wire and non-wire) and crypto (on-chain and off-chain) trades, deposits and withdrawals with a view to mitigate risk exposure to the platform, and escalate real time urgent alerts according to risk appetite.
•
Assist the Manager Transaction Monitoring in building periodic specific and general reports providing analysis that identifies ML, TF and Sanctions related anomalies for the information of the Chief Compliance Officer and relevant Product Managers.
•
As a member of the Transaction Monitoring Team, report directly to the Manager of Transaction Monitoring. Also, work closely with other Bitfinex teams and peer AML Investigators in addressing both fraud, and money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions risks.
•
In performing this role, the incumbent will continuously strive to self-develop and enhance their skill sets including the application of virtual currencies, documentation requirements, and account behavior analysis in the context of KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions.
•
Duties include understanding the framework of our transaction monitoring rules on a risk-based approach as well as analyzing and evaluating data needed to assess referrals of unusual transaction activities.
•
Ensure that KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions activities are observed at all times, issues are addressed appropriately, and matters escalated to management as required. Further, identification and/or coordination of the implementation of process improvements relating to KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions policies in conjunction with Bitfiex’s ToS as applicable are also imperative.

This role’s Tactical Responsibilities also include:

•
Initial assessment of referrals of unusual transaction activity
•
Report and analyze unusual documentation and/or information and/or query and/or transaction to/with Manager Investigations and Transaction Monitoring
•
Adjust risk parameters to ensure exposure falls within the platform’s risk appetite
•
Participate in applicable compliance training;
•
Follow and implement KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions-related policies, laws and regulations.
•
Carry out cross-departmental communication when the need arises.
•
Liaise with AML Analysts and/or users in respect of additional information required in order to verify the presence of ML/TF concerns when required.
•
Undertake evaluation and communicate findings and decisions to respective case stream team leader; escalate and/or discuss with the Head of Investigations where required.

What You Bring to the Table:
•
Experience in the compliance field within the Industry;
•
Fair understanding or ability to understand AML/KYC/CTF related policies, laws and regulations, including enhanced due diligence, (CDD/EDD) and Sanctions;
•
Basic knowledge of blockchain technology, (enhanced in the role); CAMS/CBP designation
•
​​Experience with a Blockchain Analytical/Transaction Monitoring tool such as Chainalysis, Elliptic, TRM, etc.
•
University degree
•
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
•
Ability to source and understand the content of documentation in various languages, types and forms
•
Demonstrated critical thinking and decision-making skills
•
Demonstrated attention to detail, accuracy and consistency
•
Self-motivated (ability to take initiative)
•
Proficient IT skills (Chrome, Open Search, Google Docs, Gmail, Word, Excel, etc.)
•
Organisational understanding (enhanced in the role)
•
Preferred timezones are APAC or LATAM for this position

The Role:
As a Transaction Monitoring Investigator, you will play a critical role in safeguarding the integrity of the Bitfinex platform by identifying, investigating, and mitigating financial crime risks across both fiat and cryptocurrency transactions. Working within the Compliance team, you will analyze transaction monitoring alerts, assess unusual account activity, and investigate potential money laundering, terrorist financing, sanctions, and fraud-related risks using a risk-based approach. You will collaborate closely with AML Investigators, Product teams, and Compliance leadership to ensure timely escalation of high-risk cases, contribute to regulatory reporting and process improvements, and continuously enhance monitoring controls. This role requires strong analytical thinking, sound judgment, and a deep interest in cryptocurrency, blockchain transactions, and evolving AML/KYC regulations within a fast-paced global fintech environment.

Your Day-to-Day:
•
Develop and implement transaction monitoring algorithms to monitor for anti-money laundering, terrorism financing, sanctions and other compliance risks to enable controls to be implemented to mitigate against detected risks using a risk-based approach.
•
Analyze and investigate alerts generated by the transaction monitoring system arising from fiat money (wire and non-wire) and crypto (on-chain and off-chain) trades, deposits and withdrawals with a view to mitigate risk exposure to the platform, and escalate real time urgent alerts according to risk appetite.
•
Assist the Manager Transaction Monitoring in building periodic specific and general reports providing analysis that identifies ML, TF and Sanctions related anomalies for the information of the Chief Compliance Officer and relevant Product Managers.
•
As a member of the Transaction Monitoring Team, report directly to the Manager of Transaction Monitoring. Also, work closely with other Bitfinex teams and peer AML Investigators in addressing both fraud, and money laundering, terrorist financing, and sanctions risks.
•
In performing this role, the incumbent will continuously strive to self-develop and enhance their skill sets including the application of virtual currencies, documentation requirements, and account behavior analysis in the context of KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions.
•
Duties include understanding the framework of our transaction monitoring rules on a risk-based approach as well as analyzing and evaluating data needed to assess referrals of unusual transaction activities.
•
Ensure that KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions activities are observed at all times, issues are addressed appropriately, and matters escalated to management as required. Further, identification and/or coordination of the implementation of process improvements relating to KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions policies in conjunction with Bitfiex’s ToS as applicable are also imperative.

This role’s Tactical Responsibilities also include:

•
Initial assessment of referrals of unusual transaction activity
•
Report and analyze unusual documentation and/or information and/or query and/or transaction to/with Manager Investigations and Transaction Monitoring
•
Adjust risk parameters to ensure exposure falls within the platform’s risk appetite
•
Participate in applicable compliance training;
•
Follow and implement KYC/AML/CTF and Sanctions-related policies, laws and regulations.
•
Carry out cross-departmental communication when the need arises.
•
Liaise with AML Analysts and/or users in respect of additional information required in order to verify the presence of ML/TF concerns when required.
•
Undertake evaluation and communicate findings and decisions to respective case stream team leader; escalate and/or discuss with the Head of Investigations where required.

•
Experience in the compliance field within the Industry;
•
Fair understanding or ability to understand AML/KYC/CTF related policies, laws and regulations, including enhanced due diligence, (CDD/EDD) and Sanctions;
•
Basic knowledge of blockchain technology, (enhanced in the role); CAMS/CBP designation
•
​​Experience with a Blockchain Analytical/Transaction Monitoring tool such as Chainalysis, Elliptic, TRM, etc.

University degree

Crypto.com is one of the world’s largest cryptocurrency and financial services platforms, founded in 2016 and serving customers across the globe. In the United States, Crypto.com operates a fully regulated derivatives business through Crypto.com | Derivatives North America (formerly the North American Derivatives Exchange, or Nadex) — a U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC)-regulated Designated Contract Market and Derivatives Clearing Organization headquartered in Chicago — together with its affiliated Futures Commission Merchant (FCM), Foris DAX FCM LLC.
This structure gives Crypto.com control over the full U.S. futures stack — exchange, clearing house, and broker — a regulated footprint that is rare among crypto-native firms. It places the business at the forefront of prediction markets, one of the fastest-growing and most talked-about areas in finance today, where customers can trade on the outcomes of real-world events. This is a high-growth, high-visibility business — and the Treasury function sits right at the center of it, safeguarding customer funds and ensuring the liquidity that keeps these markets running.


Role Overview
Reporting to the North America Treasurer / Head of Treasury, the Senior Treasury Analyst supports treasury-related activities for the FCM and Nadex entities, with a primary focus on cash and liquidity management. The position is critical to ensuring continuous compliance with National Futures Association (NFA) and CFTC regulatory requirements, which demand ongoing monitoring of cash balances, customer segregation, and liquidity sufficiency. This is a hybrid role: in addition to treasury, the analyst carries selected accounting and finance responsibilities, partnering closely with the Accounting and Finance teams on month-end close, reconciliations, and reporting. The role also supports the strategic growth of the derivatives and prediction markets business globally.

Key Responsibilities
• Lead daily cash and liquidity management for FCM and Nadex entities, ensuring sufficient funding to meet all customer and operational obligations.

• Continuously monitor liquidity positions to maintain compliance with NFA and CFTC requirements, including customer segregation and secured funds rules.

• Execute and oversee daily, intraday, and monthly cash movements across settlement, customer, and house accounts.

• Manage and enhance relationships with banking partners, clearing FCMs, and third-party service providers (TSPs).

• Prepare and review daily and monthly regulatory reporting for FCM and Nadex entities.

• Partner with Product and Trading teams to support expansion of derivatives offerings and ensure treasury readiness for new products.

• Support onboarding and operational readiness for Nadex direct members, including customer deposits, withdrawals, and service requests.

• Oversee reconciliation processes between trading systems and bank accounts, ensuring accuracy and timeliness.

• Lead the development and distribution of daily treasury dashboards, including performance and liquidity metrics.

• Collaborate across treasury teams to support broader Crypto.com entities and custody/vault operations.

• Identify and implement process improvements that enhance automation, control, and reporting accuracy.

Accounting & Finance Responsibilities
As a hybrid treasury, accounting, and finance role, this position also contributes to:

• Support month-end and quarter-end close activities, including journal entries, accruals, and account reconciliations related to treasury and cash operations.

• Reconcile general ledger cash and settlement accounts, ensuring activity is recorded accurately and on time.

• Partner with the Accounting and Finance teams on financial reporting, budgeting, and variance analysis.

• Help maintain internal controls and support internal and external audit requests.

Regulatory Focus (Critical)
This role plays a key part in ensuring compliance with U.S. regulatory requirements applicable to FCMs. It is a deadline-driven function with strict, recurring timelines for regulatory reporting. Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

• Continuous monitoring of customer segregated funds (CFTC 1.20, 30.7, 22.2).

• Daily verification of sufficient liquidity to meet customer obligations.

• Accurate and timely reporting to the NFA and CFTC.

• Maintenance of appropriate residual interest and liquidity buffers.

Required Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.

• 5+ years of treasury, accounting, or financial operations experience.

• Solid understanding of cash management and liquidity risk (familiarity with Futures Commission Merchant operations is helpful but can be developed on the job).

• Working knowledge of core accounting and finance processes, including the general ledger, reconciliations, and month-end close.

• Experience with process automation and improving operational efficiency.

• Experience with regulatory reporting frameworks (NFA and CFTC).

• Experience managing banking relationships and payment flows.

• Strong analytical and reconciliation skills.

• Strong attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.

• Demonstrated strong communication skills, with the ability to partner cross-functionally.

• Ability to operate in a fast-paced, highly regulated environment.

• Comfortable working to strict, recurring deadlines, particularly for time-sensitive regulatory reporting.

Preferred Qualifications
• Direct experience at an FCM, Designated Contract Market, clearing house, or derivatives clearing organization.

• Working knowledge of customer segregation rules (CFTC 1.20, 30.7, 22.2) and residual interest requirements.

• Certified Treasury Professional (CTP), Chartered Financial Analyst (CFA), or Certified Public Accountant (CPA) designation.

• Hands-on experience with a treasury management system (TMS) and advanced Microsoft Excel; experience with business intelligence (BI) tools (e.g., Tableau, Power BI) a plus.

• Exposure to digital assets, crypto markets, or other emerging financial products.

You will provide technical leadership for the software and infrastructure that form Gemini’s internal engineering platform. The Deputy Head of Transaction Monitoring is a senior 2LOD leadership role responsible for the execution, oversight, and continuous transaction monitoring framework across all regulated entities. The role sits within the Group Financial Crime & Compliance function and reports directly to the Head of Transaction Monitoring (TM).

The TM team is being built from the ground up and the Deputy Head is a foundational hire. The successful candidate will play a direct role in shaping how the function operates, establishing its culture, and setting the standard for how TM is executed across the Group. The decisions made and ways of working established in the early months of this team will define its trajectory.
The TM function is mid-build across detection capability, operating model, and platform infrastructure. The Deputy Head will drive delivery across a complex, multi-jurisdictional operating model — translating regulatory expectations into working controls, challenging first-line frameworks with credibility and precision, and providing structured, evidence-based oversight of TM risk across the Group.

All accountabilities are exercised on the direction of the Head of TM, or independently where the Head of TM is unavailable and the matter cannot be deferred without breaching a regulatory or operational obligation. The Head of TM retains ownership of the framework, regulatory relationships, and strategic decision-making. In the absence of the Head of TM, the Deputy will provide full operational continuity, maintaining oversight, escalation, and regulatory responsiveness across the Group


Responsibilities
TM Framework & Policy

• Shape and evolve the Group TM framework with the Head of TM — policies, procedures, rule design methodology, threshold calibration, and the quality assurance regime.

• Review and challenge Scenario Engineering outputs, rule specifications, threshold proposals, and back-testing results ahead of Head of TM sign-off.

• Own the quality bar for QA and Governance outputs, ensuring they meet the standard expected by senior management and regulators.

• Shape rule change proposals and threshold recalibrations through the change management process.

• Drive TM minimum standards across entities, partnering with local Heads of Compliance to close gaps.

Delegated Authority & Decision-Making
Hold formal delegated authority from the Head of TM, stepping into the primary TM decision-maker role whenever they're unavailable and a decision can't wait. In this capacity, you will:

• Approve withdrawal holds, account restrictions, and alert escalations.

• Review L3 SAR referral packs for completeness and evidential sufficiency before they go to the entity MLRO.

• Approve interim rule threshold changes that can't be deferred, recording the rationale for the Head of TM to confirm on their return.

• Deputise fully for the Head of TM during leave or absence, holding full decision-making authority within the governance framework for that period.

Regulatory Engagement
Working under the Head of TM's direction, and independently when they're unavailable, you will:

• Support the Head of TM in managing regulator relationships on TM matters.

• Respond to supervisory queries, attend regulatory meetings, and represent the TM function at inspections.

• Support the preparation and delivery of regulatory submissions, responses to supervisory feedback, and remediation communications.

• Coordinate with entity MLROs and Heads of Compliance on jurisdiction-specific TM requirements.

Team Leadership

• Provide day-to-day leadership and line management of TM specialist teams, alongside the Head of TM.

• Lead recruitment, onboarding, and development of TM analysts across pillars.

• Chair TM governance meetings, including in the Head of TM's absence.

• Act as the senior escalation point for analysts, bringing decisions to the Head of TM where needed.

• Drive risk culture across the TM function through visible leadership, consistent challenge, and clear communication.

Governance & Oversight

• Uphold the governance boundary between TM compliance decisions and commercial interests, escalating to the Group Head of Compliance and Regulatory Risk if the Head of TM is unavailable to resolve a conflict.

We are looking for a Principal Security Architect with deep crypto domain expertise to own security for the custody and on-chain layer of our regulated digital-asset platform end to end, spanning architecture, engineering, operations and regulatory assurance. Reporting into the central security function, you will define crypto-specific requirements and partner with dedicated InfraSec, AppSec, IAM and SOC teams on the platform capabilities they already own, rather than duplicating those functions. You will work closely with risk, compliance, product and engineering as we build out spot trading, custody, staking and on-chain services. This is a hands-on senior role for someone who understands that in digital-asset custody a single key-management failure is a firm-ending event, and who builds controls accordingly.


Responsibilities
• Lead end-to-end security architecture for the full custody stack: HSM/MPC key management, transaction authorization, signing quorums, address whitelisting, hot/cold wallet segregation, key ceremonies, delegated cold custodians, and secure staking deposit/withdrawal paths.

• Establish crypto-specific baseline standards, privileged-access controls, and secure SDLC requirements within our multi-account AWS environment, partnering with central InfraSec, AppSec, and IAM teams on delivery.

• Define custody and blockchain detection use cases for the SOC, and directly manage incident response procedures for crypto-specific scenarios (key compromise, unauthorized transactions, on-chain incidents) alongside Corporate Security.

• Direct security assessments and ongoing assurance for external custody providers, execution systems, blockchain analytics, Travel Rule tools, and treasury integrations using group vendor security processes.

• Own control mapping against international regulatory standards (MiCA, DORA, FCA, MAS) and collaborate with Global Market Teams to maintain compliance during international expansion.

• 10+ years in information security, with a proven track record as a security architect or technical lead securing digital-asset custody, high-throughput crypto platforms, or regulated financial infrastructure.

• Direct operational experience securing crypto custody, with deep domain expertise in wallet architecture, Multi-Party Computation (MPC), Hardware Security Modules (HSMs), key ceremonies, and signing-policy design.

• Strong cloud security fundamentals (AWS preferred) in a regulated environment, with practical experience mapping security controls to licensing conditions (ISO 27001, SOC 2, NIST).

• Demonstrated experience running threat modeling, risk assessments, and incident response, with the ability to translate technical cryptographic risk into clear business and regulatory impact for non-security teams and regulators.

• Proven comfort operating in a matrixed security model, collaborating with dedicated IAM, AppSec, SOC, and infrastructure security teams rather than owning those central functions outright.

Nice-to-Haves
•

Hands-on experience with Kubernetes, containers, Infrastructure as Code (Terraform), API security, Python for automation, Web3 dependency supply-chain assurance, or industry certifications (CISSP, CISM, CCSP, CCSSA).

•

Professional fluency in spoken and written Mandarin to support regional market operations and cross-functional engineering collaboration.

BUILDING THE FUTURE OF OPEN FINANCE


Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout,  xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.




THE TEAM

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.


We're looking for a Head of Exchange Infrastructure to own the layer every Kraken product is built on: the matching engine, core infrastructure, third-party custody, the algo engine and the API engine. Kraken grew up as a set of vertically integrated products, each with its own engine and its own APIs. This role consolidates them into a single exchange stack that serves every product and every interface. You will lead a team of four to five product managers, partnered with an engineering manager. It is a senior, independent team, which means you get leverage quickly and you are expected to stay close to the work.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own the product vision and roadmap for the exchange layer: matching engine, core infrastructure, third-party custody, algo engine and API engine

 - Lead and grow a team of four to five product managers, and set the bar for product craft across the layer

 - Lead the consolidation of multiple matching engines into one, starting with US derivatives, then international derivatives, then spot

 - Build interface-agnostic, so every product team and every interface can build on the same platform rather than their own

 - Define success metrics (p99 latency, throughput, uptime, resiliency) and hold teams accountable to them

 - Partner with engineering leaders across exchange and core infrastructure to sequence the migration without disrupting live markets

 - Partner with Risk and Credit Infrastructure so a client can hold one account and trade every product against it

 - Anticipate industry shifts and shape our platform to stay ahead

 - Align cross-functional teams (product, engineering, risk, compliance) around the exchange strategy

 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - Senior product leader with experience in exchange, trading, or high-performance platforms

 - Experience managing and developing product managers, on a team senior enough to run without you in the room

 - Happy to be a player-coach. This team is independent, so you will own roadmaps and write specs yourself at times, not only review them

 - Proven ability to set product vision and translate it into a long-term roadmap

 - Strong understanding of matching engine and market data architecture, and the tradeoffs low latency forces

 - Experience building platforms for internal customers, with the judgment to tell a platform from a series of bespoke builds

 - Excellent communication skills — can influence technical and non-technical stakeholders

 - A passion for crypto markets, market structure, and building the next generation of infrastructure

 


NICE TO HAVES

 - Engineering background before moving into product, so you've built or operated high-performance systems yourself and not just specced them

 - Experience across both spot and derivatives venues, with the market structure differences that come with each

 - Time at a crypto exchange operating at comparable scale, volume and uptime expectations

 - Track record building platform roadmaps that interlock with adjacent product orgs rather than running in isolation







Unless a specific application deadline is stated in the job posting, applications are accepted on an ongoing basis.

Please note, applicants are permitted to redact or remove information on their resume that identifies age, date of birth, or dates of attendance at or graduation from an educational institution.

We consider qualified applicants with criminal histories for employment on our team, assessing candidates in a manner consistent with the requirements of the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance.




OUR COMMITMENT

Payward is powered by people from around the world and we celebrate the diverse talents, backgrounds, contributions, and unique perspectives that everyone brings to the table. We hire based on merit, seeking out people with the right abilities, knowledge, and skills for the job. We encourage you to apply for roles where you don't fully meet the listed requirements, especially if you're passionate or knowledgeable about crypto.


We may ask candidates to complete job-related skills or work-style assessments as part of our hiring process. These assessments evaluate competencies relevant to the role and are applied consistently across candidates for similar positions. Results are considered alongside experience and interviews, and are not the sole basis for any employment decision.


As an equal opportunity employer, we don't tolerate discrimination or harassment of any kind, whether based on race, ethnicity, age, gender identity, citizenship, religion, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic as outlined by federal, state, or local laws.

Learn on the Kraken Blog https://blog.kraken.com/#:~:text=Enter%20your%20email%20address

Connect on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/kraken-exchange/

About the Opportunity

OKX is going all-in on AI-native localisation. The field has long been stuck on one trade-off: you can have translation quality, or you can have scale, but not both. And the real question was never "is this translation accurate?" — it's "can the user actually understand it and get through the flow?"

Web3 is the hardest place to solve this. The vocabulary reinvents itself constantly, with new tech jargon, protocol names and memes appearing every week. It sits next to dense, high-stakes trading terminology, where a single mistranslated word can mislead a user or move money. And every market has its own fast-moving regulations, so the "right" translation is a moving target that must stay compliant across jurisdictions in real time. If you want a localisation problem that is genuinely unsolved — high ambiguity, high stakes, high velocity — this is it.

We're going to break the trade-off with agents. You will own the 0-1 build and launch of two things:

•

A frontier agentic translation system that localises every market (20+ languages) with a human-in-the-loop mechanism.

•

A self-improving agentic QA product that autonomously evaluates translation and end-to-end localisation quality, flags its own failures, and closes the loop.

This is a build-the-frontier role, not a manage-the-vendor role.

This role does not require a linguistics or translation background, multilingual ability, or algorithm engineering skills. We're looking for a PM leader who can build a frontier agentic translation and QA system from 0 to 1 — and make the whole organisation share responsibility for localisation quality.

What You’ll Be Doing

You will lead a squad of product managers and developers, and work hand-in-hand with language managers, to ship the translation and QA systems into production. You set the product direction and quality bar; your PMs and engineers build the agents, harness and evals; and the language managers ground the system in what "good" actually means in each market. Your job is to make these three groups operate as one team — and to make localisation quality something the whole organisation owns, not just the language team.

Own the agentic translation system

Architect and ship it end to end, from 0 to 1, across all markets and 20+ languages — where models carry the work and humans set the standard and make the final call. Break the cost curve: hold quality flat while coverage scales across languages, content and release velocity, so cost stops growing linearly with the business. Make the system interoperate cleanly with OKX's existing localisation stack and content pipelines, rather than living as an island.

Build the agentic QA and quality automation

Stand up an autonomous QA agent that evaluates translation and localisation quality at scale — catching regressions before release, monitoring in production, and self-verifying every fix, using LLM-as-a-judge and eval harnesses rather than manual review. Evaluate not just accuracy and fluency but cultural fit, bias and safety — especially on regulated and financial content, where a wrong or non-compliant phrasing is a real risk. Make quality measurable: define and drive a hard quality signal — human-acceptance rate, or the edit effort needed to reach shippable quality (e.g. Translation Time-to-Edit) — so quality is a metric the system optimises against, not a subjective call. Own complex, high-stakes journeys end to end across account, assets, compliance, or support, taking them from problem definition to shipped, polished execution.

• Maintain the regulatory change log, assess the impact of each development on the relevant entity, and assign owners, actions and deadlines.
• Summarise changes in plain English for senior management and for non-compliance colleagues, and present updates at the relevant governance forums.

• Carry out monitoring reviews and thematic testing to the agreed schedule, gathering evidence, testing samples and documenting results to a standard that will withstand regulatory and audit scrutiny.
• Write up findings, agree remedial actions with the business, and track those actions through to closure.
• Report on CMP progress, overdue actions and emerging risks to the Compliance Team and relevant committees.
• Support audits, regulatory visits, information requests and third party due diligence questionnaires.
Wider compliance support
• Provide second line advice and challenge to first line teams on conduct, treating customers fairly and consumer duty style obligations, and on financial promotions.
• Support financial crime activity where required, including AML and CTF, sanctions, PEP screening, Market Abuse Surveillance, Transaction Monitoring and escalation to the MLRO.

Job Description
As the Head of Internal Audit, you will lead the Group’s independent Internal Audit function, providing objective assurance and strategic insight on the effectiveness of Swissquote’s governance, risk management and internal control framework.
Reporting directly to the Board of Directors and its Audit & Risk Committee, the role oversees the Internal Audit function across the Swissquote Group, defining a risk-based audit strategy and ensuring appropriate coverage of financial, regulatory, operational, technology and emerging risks.
As the Bank transitions from Category 4 to Category 3 under FINMA's banking categorization, Swissquote will internalize the Internal Audit function currently performed by an external provider. The objective is to broaden the risk assessment expertise, audit planning and internal audit governance in-house, while retaining the flexibility and specialist expertise of external providers through a co-sourced internal audit model.
The Head of Internal Audit will lead the internalization process and build the function from the ground up, including its governance, charter, methodology, team, tools and audit universe. The role will ensure a smooth transition from the outgoing external partner and full compliance with FINMA requirements applicable to a Category 3 institution.
Acting as a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders, the Head of Internal Audit will maintain the highest standards of independence, professional scepticism and integrity while contributing to the continuous strengthening of Swissquote’s governance and control environment.
This position is a highly visible, build-and-lead mandate, with direct exposure to the Board of Directors and Audit Committee.
Key Responsibilities:
Internal Audit Strategy & Governance
• Define and maintain the Internal Audit strategy, methodology and multi-year audit plan, aligned with Swissquote's business model, risk profile and regulatory requirements.
• Establish, maintain and periodically review the Internal Audit Charter and ensure Board approval and alignment with regulatory and professional standards.
• Develop a risk-based audit universe and annual audit plan, ensuring appropriate coverage of material financial, operational, technological and regulatory risks.
• Ensure that Internal Audit operates in accordance with applicable FINMA requirements and recognised professional standards.
• Regularly assess the effectiveness and adequacy of the Internal Audit framework and continuously improve its methodology, tools and processes.
• Maintain an appropriate level of independence from the activities and functions being audited.
• Establish safeguards ensuring objectivity and independence of the Internal Audit function and address any actual, potential or perceived impairments.
• Lead and personally perform selected audits in areas where the Head of Internal Audit’s expertise is most relevant or where the use of external resources is not justified by risk, complexity, or cost.
• Maintain overall accountability for the quality, supervision and reliance placed on work performed by co-sourcing partners and external specialists.
• Across the years, progressively build and develop the Internal Audit team in line with the evolution of the function and the organisation’s risk profile, with strong emphasis on internal development, cross-functional exposure and the development of future audit talent. Establish a clear vision for a lean and digitally enabled Internal Audit function, including the development of data analytics, IT audit capabilities, automated monitoring and management dashboards.
• Design, implement and maintain a Quality Assurance and Improvement Program (QAIP) covering internal and external assessments, performance measurement and continuous improvement of the Internal Audit function and ensure the QAIP is assessed in accordance with Global Internal Audit Standards.
• Develop and manage the Internal Audit budget and resource plan, ensuring sufficient capabilities and capacity to fulfil the approved audit plan.
• Establish and report performance metrics demonstrating the effectiveness, efficiency and value contribution of Internal Audit.
Risk & Control Assurance
• Provide independent assurance to the Board and Executive Management on the effectiveness of Swissquote's governance, risk management and internal control framework, through a risk-based and forward-looking audit approach.
• Lead the assessment of risks across the organisation and ensure that the Internal Audit plan evolves in line with Swissquote's risk profile and business strategy.
• Challenge management constructively on significant control weaknesses, risk exposures and remediation plans, ensuring that material findings are appropriately addressed and escalated when necessary.
Board and Audit & Risk Committee
• Act as the primary Internal Audit advisor to the Board of Directors and its Audit & Risk Committee, providing an independent view on the overall effectiveness of Swissquote's governance, risk management and control environment.
• Present and discuss the Internal Audit Charter, the Internal Audit strategy, annual plan, key findings, emerging risk themes and QIAP.
Regulatory & External Stakeholder Management
• Maintain a constructive relationship with FINMA, the external audit firm and other relevant regulatory stakeholders.
• Coordinate, where appropriate, with external audit and other assurance functions (internal and external) to ensure appropriate coverage and avoid unnecessary duplication.
• Ensure that Internal Audit is prepared to respond effectively to regulatory reviews and supervisory expectations.
• Monitor regulatory developments and assess their implications for the Internal Audit plan.
Digital & Technology Audit
• Ensure adequate audit coverage of IT architecture, applications, infrastructure and technology governance.
• Assess cybersecurity, identity and access management, data management and technology resilience.
• Review the governance and control environment surrounding AI and emerging technologies.
• AI fluency, with demonstrated experience, a strong sensitivity to AI-related topics, and the ability to confidently assess and challenge AI-generated outputs.
• Develop appropriate use of data analytics and automation within Internal Audit.
• Ensure Internal Audit evolves alongside Swissquote's technology and digital transformation.
People Leadership
• Build, lead, develop and motivate the Internal Audit team and foster a strong culture of professional scepticism, independence, integrity and continuous improvement.
• Attract, develop, and retain top talents while ensuring clear roles, performance goals, and career progression paths.
• Ensure appropriate professional development and certification of Internal Audit professionals.

Qualifications
Education & Professional Qualifications
• Master's degree or equivalent in Finance, Accounting, Economics, Business Administration, Law or another relevant discipline from a recognised university.
• Professional Internal Audit qualification, Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) or Federal Diploma as a Certified Public Accountant (CPA) is a must.
• In-depth knowledge of the Swiss banking regulatory environment and FINMA requirements, particularly in relation to corporate governance, risk management, internal controls and Internal Audit.
• Ability to assess the effectiveness, scope, documentation, and lessons learned from the previously outsourced internal audit model.
• Build strong working relationships with senior management while reinforcing the independent role of internal audit.
• Strong understanding of international banking regulation and recognised industry practices.
• Excellent analytical, communication, report-writing, stakeholder management, and influencing skills.
• High level of integrity, independence, professional judgment, and discretion.
• Strong business acumen with the ability to identify emerging strategic, operational, financial, and compliance risks.
• English is a must, French and German an asset.
Professional Experience

Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 80 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance.

Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution.

Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services.

Key Responsibilities:

•

Assess the Status Quo — Develop an end-to-end understanding of the campaign lifecycle and available data assets; identify all decision points currently reliant on manual judgment (opportunity identification, audience selection, budget estimation, campaign mechanics design, post-campaign review) and determine where intelligent automation yields the highest return.

•

What Campaign to Run — Mine campaign opportunities from user behavior, product and market signals, and historical campaign performance; build an AI Agent that outputs candidate campaign themes with clear supporting evidence, not just a ranked list.

•

Who to Target — Build or reuse user segmentation and response/propensity models; apply uplift modeling to direct budget toward truly incremental audiences who would be influenced, rather than users who would convert anyway.

•

How Much Budget — Build a cost-benefit model: projected participation, incremental trading volume / revenue, ROI simulation, budget allocation recommendations, and sensitivity and risk analysis (including abuse and reward-farming risks under incentive designs).

•

Feasibility Analysis & Plan Design — Translate model outputs into a reviewable proposal: objectives, mechanics, target audience, budget, expected KPIs, and risk control boundaries; align with PM, Growth, and business stakeholders.

•

MVP Delivery — Implement the end-to-end pipeline (data → model → recommendation → campaign configuration → A/B or holdout evaluation); run it on at least one real campaign or rigorous backtest; quantify improvement relative to the current manual decision-making baseline.

Requirements:

•

Undergraduate or graduate student in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Economics, or a related field.

•

Solid proficiency in SQL and Python. Experience with real-time / streaming tech stacks (Flink, Kafka) is a plus.

•

Data science foundations relevant to this project: A/B experiment design, causal inference and uplift modeling, propensity/response models, and basic predictive modeling. Must be able to distinguish correlation from incremental effect.

•

Hands-on experience with LLM application development: prompt engineering, RAG, Agent / tool-calling frameworks; able to use LLMs for reasoning and orchestration on top of quantitative models.

•

Business acumen: genuine interest in fintech / crypto and growth marketing; able to translate a business question ("Should we run a trading competition next month?") into a data problem, and translate the conclusion back into an actionable decision for business stakeholders.

•

Strong communication skills — this role sits at the intersection of data, PM, and growth/marketing.

•

Bonus: experience in growth / CRM / campaign analytics, recommendation systems, or marketing mix modeling background.

•

Minimum 3-month internship commitment, 5 days per week on-site.

•

Fluent in Mandarin is required.

• Represent OG.com on a variety of topics with the SEC.

• Reviewing marketing and sales literature, presentations, and other educational materials for compliance with applicable SEC laws and regulations.

• Work with external counsel to ensure our arrangements comply with relevant law and regulation in jurisdictions where we operate.

• Qualified/licensed lawyer with 3 to 5 years of experience in financial product legal and regulatory work handling issues for SEC-regulated clients in a major law firm or as a licensed entity (broker-dealer or national securities exchange) or at the SEC.

• Excellent knowledge of US financial laws and regulatory structures and track record of maintaining licenses and building products and operations under these frameworks, as well as the cross-border interaction of these laws and regulatory structures.

• Familiarity with industry practices and professional standards.

• Excellent English verbal and written communication skills.

• Strong organizational/project management skills, ability to handle high volume and balance competing demands.

 - Support leadership in decision-making by framing issues, tracking KPIs, and surfacing gaps or risks early.

 - Maintain systems for reporting, business reviews, roadmap coordination, and cross-team initiatives.

 - Partner with leadership to scope and stand up new initiatives in Spot, Margin, Derivatives, or Infrastructure — from early concept through initial execution.

 - Contribute to high-impact materials (exec updates, all-hands, strategic memos) that provide clarity and visibility.

 - Act as the first line of intake for inbound requests, triage them effectively, and ensure accountability for follow-through.

 - Identify bottlenecks in how we operate and propose improvements that help the team scale more efficiently.

 - Use business intelligence and data to support PMs and leadership across Pro, cutting through competing priorities and surface the best opportunities.

 - Partner with Compliance and Legal teams to find ways to improve product experience.

 
 


WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5–7 years in BizOps, Product Ops, Strategy, Consulting, or similar high-leverage roles with measurable impact.

 - Strong project management skills — you can bring structure to ambiguity and drive initiatives from 0 → 1.

 - Comfortable with data: you can interpret dashboards, KPIs, and financial/operational metrics to drive insight.

 - Excellent communicator who can adapt across audiences — from execs to cross-functional ICs.

 - Highly organized, detail-driven, and biased toward follow-through and execution.

 - Self-starter who doesn’t wait for instructions — you create the roadmap when one doesn’t exist.

 - Experience collaborating across product, engineering, compliance, legal, finance, and marketing.

 - Belief in Kraken’s mission to accelerate financial freedom and inclusion through crypto.

About the Opportunity:
 
The HR Business Partner (HRBP) Leader is a strategic role responsible for aligning HR initiatives with the organization's business objectives. This position partners with senior leadership to drive talent strategies, foster a high-performance culture, and support organizational growth and transformation. The HRBP Leader oversees a team of HRBPs, ensuring the delivery of comprehensive HR solutions, including talent management, employee engagement, organizational development, and workforce planning.
 


Responsibilities:
•

Strategic Partnership: Collaborate with senior leadership to understand business goals and translate them into HR strategies that drive performance, employee engagement, and organizational success.

•

Team Leadership & Cross-Functional Collaboration: Guide the existing HRBP team member, and actively initiate and co-work with regional HR specialists to handle complex employee relations issues and cases.

•

Talent Management: Oversee succession planning, leadership development, and performance management processes to build a robust talent pipeline across business units.

•

Employee Engagement: Drive initiatives to enhance employee experience, including engagement surveys, action planning, and programs to promote inclusion, diversity, equity, and belonging.

•

Change Management: Lead organizational change initiatives, including restructures, mergers, or cultural transformations, ensuring effective communication and minimal disruption.

•

Workforce Planning: Partner with leadership to forecast workforce needs, develop staffing strategies, and align resources with business priorities.

•

HR Metrics & Analytics: Utilize data-driven insights to assess HR program effectiveness, monitor key metrics (e.g., turnover, engagement, time-to-hire), and make informed recommendations.

•

Policy & Compliance: Partner with HR Ops to ensure HR practices within business units comply with local labor laws and internal policies, while promoting fairness and consistency.

•

The role will have particular responsibility for supporting cross-border payment flows, including monitoring settlement across different markets, currencies, banking/payment partners and transaction channels.

Reconciliation Management

• Own the end-to-end reconciliation process across all relevant transaction and payment channels.
• Perform daily reconciliation of customer transactions against internal ledgers, bank accounts, wallets and payment/settlement partner records.

• Ensure all transactions are accurately recorded, accounted for and appropriately classified.
• Identify reconciliation breaks, unmatched transactions, duplicate transactions, missing entries and other discrepancies.
• Investigate and resolve reconciliation exceptions within defined timelines.
• Maintain accurate reconciliation schedules and supporting documentation.
• Ensure outstanding reconciliation items are properly tracked through to resolution.
• Develop and maintain reconciliation controls to minimise financial leakage and operational errors.

Settlement Management

• Own and coordinate settlement processes across banking, payment and liquidity partners.
• Ensure settlements are completed accurately and within agreed timelines.
• Monitor settlement positions across currencies, accounts and payment channels.
• Coordinate settlement instructions and confirmations with relevant internal and external stakeholders.

• Identify settlement risks and escalate material issues appropriately.

Cross-Border Payments

• Manage reconciliation and settlement processes associated with cross-border payment transactions.
• Monitor movement of funds across different currencies, jurisdictions, banking partners and payment channels.
• Reconcile inbound and outbound cross-border transactions across relevant accounts and systems.
• Track transaction status from initiation through processing, settlement and final reconciliation.
• Investigate discrepancies arising from FX conversion, fees, exchange-rate differences, intermediary charges, timing differences and settlement delays.
• Work with banking and payment partners to resolve cross-border settlement issues.
• Monitor foreign exchange and settlement costs and identify opportunities to improve efficiency.
• Maintain appropriate records for cross-border transactions and support required operational and regulatory reporting.

Partner & Banking Operations

• Manage operational relationships with banks, payment service providers, liquidity providers and other settlement partners.
• Monitor partner balances, settlement accounts and transaction positions.
• Validate partner statements and settlement reports against internal records.
• Investigate partner discrepancies and coordinate resolution.
• Monitor agreed SLAs and settlement performance.
• Support the onboarding and integration of new payment and settlement partners from a reconciliation and settlement perspective.
• Maintain a clear record of partner-specific settlement processes and requirements.

Exception Management

• Establish and maintain an effective exception management process.
• Monitor unresolved reconciliation and settlement exceptions.
• Categorise exceptions according to value, risk, age and root cause.
• Escalate high-value, unusual or prolonged exceptions.
• Conduct root-cause analysis of recurring reconciliation and settlement issues.
• Work with Product, Engineering, Operations, Finance and external partners to resolve systemic issues.
• Recommend process or system improvements to reduce recurring exceptions.

Treasury & Liquidity Coordination

• Monitor operational balances required to support settlement and payment obligations.
• Identify potential liquidity gaps or excess balances across accounts and currencies.

• Support liquidity planning for cross-border payment corridors.
• Monitor currency exposures and settlement requirements.
• Provide timely information to Finance and management to support liquidity decisions.

• Monitor transactions and settlement processes for operational risks and potential financial losses.
• Work closely with Risk and Compliance on issues relating to transaction integrity, suspicious activity, fraud risks and regulatory requirements.
• Ensure appropriate approval and authorisation controls are followed.

• Maintain appropriate records and evidence for all material financial movements.

Nice to Have

• Proven experience scaling and enhancing AI products or solutions, including taking existing AI applications, code, or technologies and expanding their usage across teams, markets, or the wider organisation.

• Strong technical experience with Python, LLMs, APIs, databases, and AI platforms/tools.
